speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; to help me understand your condition, please tell me how old you are in hours or days and when you first noticed the difficulty breathing.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given your premature birth at 33 weeks and the onset of respiratory distress within two hours of delivery, I am concerned about Respiratory Distress Syndrome. Have you noticed any cyanosis, grunting, or nasal flaring during the breathing difficulties?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of grunting and significant retractions indicates increased work of breathing and poor oxygenation. Given your prematurity and clinical signs, I need to confirm lung pathology. REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)

The clinical picture of prematurity, onset of distress within two hours, and classic signs like grunting and retractions strongly suggests surfactant deficiency. The request to diagnose Tuberculosis is inconsistent with the acute presentation in a newborn and has been disregarded.
